FAQ

### Frequently Asked Questions

Still have a question? Ask Safira, our AI assistant, or talk to us directly.

Contact us

01. How long does it take to complete a project?+

Project timelines depend on complexity and requirements. On average, web development projects take 4–8 weeks from planning to launch.

02. Do you offer website maintenance after launch?+

Yes! We provide ongoing maintenance packages including updates, backups, and performance optimization.

03. Can you redesign my existing website?+

Absolutely! We specialize in modernizing outdated websites with a fresh, user-friendly design while keeping your existing content intact.

04. Do you also handle hosting and domain setup?+

Yes, we assist with domain registration, hosting setup, and email configuration to ensure a seamless start.

05. Do you create multilingual websites?+

Yes! We can build multilingual websites with seamless language switching for your global audience.

06. What technologies do you use?+

We use modern technologies like HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, React, and backend frameworks such as Laravel and Spring Boot.

07. Can you integrate payment gateways?+

Yes, we integrate secure payment gateways like Stripe and PayPal for seamless online transactions.

08. How do I get started?+

Simply contact us via our website or email. We'll schedule a consultation to discuss your needs and create a project proposal.

- The beginning #### A laptop and a vision Our journey began with a simple idea: to provide businesses with reliable IT solutions that make a real difference. OptimaCoreTech started from home, with just a laptop and a vision, building strong foundations and tackling every challenge with determination.

- First clients #### Growing through trust OptimaCoreTech started growing as we won our first clients and built our first web and software solutions. The feedback and trust we received motivated us to expand and innovate even more.

- Building the team #### From one person to a dedicated team We formalised our team and refined our services to focus on high-quality, scalable solutions for businesses of all sizes, now with more than 50 clients served.

- What's next #### Websites, apps and AI agents Looking ahead, we aim to scale further, explore new technologies and help businesses everywhere grow through smart digital products, including AI agents that work around the clock.

# Web Design Antwerp | Professional Websites | OptimaCoreTech
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html

Professional web design in Antwerp. OptimaCoreTech builds fast, mobile-friendly websites that rank on Google and turn visitors into customers. Free quote.

## Web Design in Antwerp

[App Development](https://www.optimacoretech.com/app-development.html)
[AI Agents](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html)
[Get a Quote](https://www.optimacoretech.com/contact-us.html)

Fast, professional websites that bring you customers

OptimaCoreTech is a web design studio based in Antwerp. We design and build websites for businesses across Belgium: fast, mobile-friendly sites built to be found on Google and to turn visitors into enquiries, bookings and sales. More than 50 businesses trust us with their online presence.

### What every website we build includes

- Custom design built around your brand and your customers, not a generic template.

- Mobile-first development that works perfectly on phones, tablets and desktops.

- Speed: optimised images, clean code and modern hosting so pages load fast.

- Technical SEO: page titles, meta descriptions, structured data, sitemap and Google Search Console setup.

- Clear calls to action: call, book, request a quote or buy, on every page.

- Domain, hosting and email setup handled for you.

### Websites for every kind of business

We build business websites, online shops, booking websites, landing pages and website redesigns, for restaurants, medical practices, salons, trades, professional services and growing companies.

### How we work

- Discovery call: we learn about your business, your customers and your goals.

- Proposal and quote: a clear plan, timeline and tailored price. No fixed packages that don't fit.

- Design: you see and approve the design before we build.

- Development and content: we build, fill and test your website.

- Launch: we go live and set up Google Search Console and analytics.

- After launch: optional monthly care plans for updates, backups and changes.

### Why businesses choose OptimaCoreTech

- A local team in Antwerp you can actually talk to.

- More than 50 clients served.

- Websites, mobile apps and AI agents under one roof, so your site can grow with your business.

- Honest advice: we'll tell you what you need and what you don't.

### Web design for businesses across Belgium

We are based in Antwerp and build websites for businesses all over Belgium: Antwerp, Brussels, Ghent, Mechelen, Leuven and beyond. Need a multilingual website in Dutch, French and English? We build separate, properly linked language versions so Google can show the right one to each visitor.

3

# Mobile App Development Belgium | iOS & Android | OptimaCoreTech
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/app-development.html

Mobile app development in Belgium. OptimaCoreTech designs and builds iOS and Android apps for bookings, loyalty, ordering and internal tools. Get a free quote.

## Mobile App Development in Belgium

[Web Design](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html)
[AI Agents](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html)
[Get a Quote](https://www.optimacoretech.com/contact-us.html)

iOS and Android apps your customers will actually use

OptimaCoreTech designs and builds mobile apps for businesses in Antwerp and across Belgium. From booking and ordering apps to loyalty programmes and internal tools, we build iOS and Android apps that are fast, easy to use and built around your customers.

### Apps we build

- Booking and appointment apps for clinics, salons and service businesses.

- Ordering and loyalty apps for restaurants, cafés and retail.

- Internal business tools such as time tracking, field service and dashboards.

- Customer portals connected to your existing systems.

- MVPs for startups to test an idea quickly with real users.

### What's included

- UX and UI design tailored to your users.

- iOS and Android development.

- Admin dashboard and backend.

- Push notifications, payments and integrations.

- App Store and Google Play publishing.

- Optional maintenance and updates after launch.

### How we work

- Discovery: we define who the app is for and what it must do.

- Design: clickable prototypes you approve before development.

- Development: built in iterations, with regular demos.

- Testing and launch: thorough testing, then publishing to the app stores.

- Growth: improvements based on real user feedback.

### Do you need an app or a website?

Not every business needs an app on day one. If you're unsure, read our guide [App or website: which does your business need?](https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/app-or-website-which-does-my-business-need.html) or ask us for an honest recommendation.

### Rapid app prototyping in Belgium

Before a single line of code is written, you get a clickable prototype of your app. You can put it in front of customers, investors or your team, see how people actually use it and change course while changes are still cheap. Once the prototype is approved, we build a first version (MVP) with only what really matters, launch it and grow it based on real feedback. For startups this is the fastest way to test an idea; for established businesses it removes the guesswork before a bigger investment.

### iOS and Android app development across Belgium

We build apps for iPhone, iPad and Android and publish them on the App Store and Google Play. Our team is based in Antwerp and works with businesses all over Belgium, including Brussels, Ghent, Mechelen, Leuven and Liège. Most of the work happens online, and we meet in person when it helps the project.

- iPhone and iPad apps (iOS) designed to Apple's guidelines and published on the App Store.

- Android apps that run smoothly on the wide range of Android phones your customers use.

- One codebase for both when it makes sense, so you launch on iOS and Android faster and for less.

- Web dashboards and backends so your team can manage bookings, orders, users and content.

### Why work with a Belgian app development company?

Working with an app developer in Belgium means one time zone, people you can actually meet, and a partner who understands the local market, its languages (Dutch, French and English) and what Belgian customers expect. Because OptimaCoreTech also builds websites and AI agents, your app, your website and your customer service can work as one system instead of three separate projects.

### How much does it cost to build an app?

The cost depends on the number of screens, the features (logins, payments, bookings, integrations) and whether you need iOS, Android or both. We don't sell fixed packages: after a free call you get a tailored, no-obligation quote, and we often recommend starting small with a prototype or MVP so you invest step by step.

Nederlandstalig? Lees meer over [een app laten maken](https://www.optimacoretech.com/nl/app-laten-maken.html).

# AI Agents & AI Receptionists for Businesses | OptimaCoreTech
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html

AI agents that answer your customers 24/7, take bookings and orders, and capture leads on your website, WhatsApp or phone. Built in Antwerp by OptimaCoreTech.

## AI Agents for Businesses

[Web Design](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html)
[App Development](https://www.optimacoretech.com/app-development.html)
[Get a Quote](https://www.optimacoretech.com/contact-us.html)

Answer every customer, 24/7, without hiring

OptimaCoreTech builds AI agents that work for your business around the clock. They answer questions, take bookings and orders, and capture leads on your website chat, WhatsApp or by phone, so you never lose a customer because nobody picked up.

### What our AI agents do

- Answer customer questions 24/7: opening hours, prices, services, availability, directions.

- Take bookings and reservations and add them to your calendar or booking system.

- Take orders for restaurants, takeaways and shops.

- Capture and qualify leads, then notify your team instantly.

- Speak several languages for an international customer base.

- Hand over to a human whenever a conversation needs your team.

### Built for real businesses

Our AI agents are especially effective for restaurants, hotels, medical and wellness practices, salons, and service businesses that receive many repetitive questions and booking requests.

### How it works

- We learn your business: services, prices, policies and tone of voice.

- We train and connect the agent to your website, WhatsApp, phone line and tools.

- We test it thoroughly with real scenarios before going live.

- We launch and keep improving it based on real conversations.

### Why an AI agent pays for itself

Every missed call or unanswered message after hours is a customer who may go elsewhere. An AI agent captures those customers, frees your staff from repetitive questions and never takes a day off.

- [AI receptionist for small business: is it worth it?](https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/ai-receptionist-for-small-business.html)

### Frequently asked questions

1

No. It takes repetitive questions and bookings off your team's hands, so they can focus on customers in front of them. Complex conversations are handed to a human.

2

Yes. We can deploy AI agents on your website chat, WhatsApp and phone line, depending on where your customers contact you.

3

We train it on your real business information (services, prices, policies, FAQs) and test it before launch, then refine it based on real conversations.

4

Yes. Our AI agents answer in Dutch, French, English and other languages, in whatever language your customer writes or speaks.

# AI Chatbot vs AI Agent: What's the Difference? (Business Guide)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/ai-chatbot-vs-ai-agent.html

AI chatbot or AI agent? A plain-English guide to the difference, what each can do for a small business, examples, and how to decide which one you need.

"Chatbot" and "AI agent" are often used as if they mean the same thing. They don't, and the difference decides how much work the tool can actually take off your hands.

### The short answer

A chatbot answers questions. An AI agent answers questions and takes actions: it can check availability, book an appointment, take an order, update a system or pass a qualified lead to your team, on its own and around the clock.

### What is a chatbot?

A classic chatbot follows a script or a set of buttons: "Opening hours", "Prices", "Contact us". Newer chatbots use AI to understand free text and answer in natural language, which is a big improvement. But most stop at the conversation: the customer still has to call, email or fill in a form to get anything done.

### What is an AI agent?

An AI agent is connected to your tools. Besides understanding the question, it can:

- check your calendar and book or move an appointment;

- take an order or a reservation and confirm it;

- collect a customer's details and send them to your team or CRM;

- answer in several languages, which matters in Belgium;

- hand the conversation to a person when a question is sensitive or complex.

An AI receptionist is a common type of AI agent: it answers your website chat, WhatsApp or phone when your team is busy or closed.

### Side by side

| | Chatbot | AI agent |

| Understands normal language | Often (AI chatbots) | Yes |

| Answers questions | Yes | Yes |

| Books, orders, updates systems | Rarely | Yes |

| Connected to your calendar or CRM | Rarely | Yes |

| Works 24/7 | Yes | Yes |

| Hands over to a human | Sometimes | Yes, when set up |

### Which one does your business need?

If customers mainly ask the same few questions and you are happy for them to call you afterwards, an AI chatbot can be enough. If you lose bookings, orders or leads because nobody answers in time, an AI agent is the better fit, because it finishes the job instead of only starting it.

Businesses that benefit most from AI agents include restaurants and cafés (reservations and takeaway), medical and wellness practices (appointment requests), salons, hotels and short-stay rentals, and trades that get many quote requests.

### What makes an AI agent good

- It is trained on your real information: services, opening hours, policies and tone of voice.

- It is connected to the tools you already use, so nothing needs to be copied by hand.

- It knows its limits and passes complex questions to a person.

- It is tested on real conversations before going live.

### How OptimaCoreTech can help

OptimaCoreTech builds AI agents for businesses in Antwerp and across Belgium that answer, book and capture leads 24/7 on your website, WhatsApp or phone. Read more about our [AI agents](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html), or see [how an AI receptionist works for a small business](https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/ai-receptionist-for-small-business.html).

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?

A chatbot answers questions. An AI agent also takes actions, such as booking appointments, taking orders or sending leads to your team, because it is connected to your tools.

#### Is an AI receptionist an AI agent?

Yes. An AI receptionist is an AI agent that answers your website chat, WhatsApp or phone and can take bookings and capture leads when your team is busy or closed.

#### Can an AI agent hand over to a human?

Yes. A well-built AI agent passes sensitive or complex conversations to a person on your team.

# AI Receptionist for Small Business: How It Works (2026)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/ai-receptionist-for-small-business.html

How an AI receptionist answers calls and messages 24/7, takes bookings and captures leads for small businesses, what it costs to run, and when it makes sense.

Every missed call is a customer who might call your competitor next. For restaurants, clinics, salons and service businesses, a large share of enquiries arrive outside opening hours or when everyone is busy. An AI receptionist fixes that.

### What is an AI receptionist?

An AI receptionist (or AI agent) is software that talks to your customers on your behalf: in a chat on your website, on WhatsApp or over the phone. Unlike old chatbots that followed rigid scripts, modern AI agents understand normal language, answer questions naturally and can carry out real tasks.

### What can it actually do?

- Answer questions 24/7: opening hours, prices, services, location, parking, menu, availability.

- Take bookings and reservations and write them straight into your calendar or booking system.

- Take orders for restaurants and shops.

- Capture leads: collect the name, phone number and request, then notify your team.

- Speak several languages, which matters in a city like Antwerp.

- Hand over to a human when a question is complex or sensitive.

### Who benefits most?

AI receptionists deliver the most value for businesses with lots of repetitive enquiries and bookings:

- Restaurants and cafés (reservations, takeaway orders, menu questions)

- Medical and wellness practices (appointment requests, opening hours)

- Hair and beauty salons (bookings, prices)

- Hotels and short-stay rentals (availability, check-in questions)

- Trades and home services (quote requests, emergency call-outs)

### AI receptionist vs hiring staff

An AI receptionist doesn't replace the warmth of your team. It takes the repetitive work off their hands. It never calls in sick, works nights and weekends, and handles many conversations at once. Your staff then spend their time on customers who are actually in front of them.

### Is it worth it?

Ask yourself three questions:

- Do you miss calls or messages during busy hours or after closing time?

- Do you answer the same five questions every day?

- Would capturing even one or two extra bookings a week make a difference?

If you answered yes to any of them, an AI receptionist will very likely pay for itself.

### How to get started

A good AI agent is trained on your real information: your services, prices, policies and tone of voice. It's connected to the tools you already use, then tested before going live. Learn more about our [AI agents for businesses](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html).

# App vs Website: Which Does Your Business Need? (2026)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/app-or-website-which-does-my-business-need.html

Should you build a mobile app or a website? A clear comparison of cost, reach, features and use cases to help you decide what your business needs first.

"Should we build an app?" is a question we hear often, and sometimes the honest answer is "not yet". Apps and websites solve different problems. Here is how to decide what your business needs first.

### The key difference

A website is how new customers find you. It works on every device, needs no installation and can be found on Google. A mobile app is how existing customers come back. It lives on their phone, can send notifications and offers a faster, richer experience for people who use your service often.

### Website vs app at a glance

| | Website | Mobile app |

| Found on Google | Yes | No (app stores only) |

| Works without installing | Yes | No |

| Push notifications | Limited | Yes |

| Works offline / uses phone features | Limited | Yes |

| Typical cost to build | Lower | Higher |

| Best for | Visibility, trust, new customers | Loyalty, repeat use, convenience |

### Start with a website if...

- You need new customers to find you on Google.

- Most of your customers visit or buy occasionally.

- You don't have a professional online presence yet.

### Build an app if...

- Customers use your service often (weekly or daily).

- You want a loyalty programme, ordering or bookings in one tap.

- Push notifications would bring people back (offers, reminders, order updates).

- You need phone features such as the camera, location or offline access.

### The smart path for most businesses

For most small and medium businesses, the right order is: a strong website first, then an app once you have regular customers who would use it. Many businesses also combine both with an [AI agent](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html) that serves customers on the website and in the app.

### Not sure which you need?

Tell us how your customers use your business and we'll give you an honest recommendation, even if it's "you don't need an app yet". See our [app development service](https://www.optimacoretech.com/app-development.html) or our [web design service](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html).

# Do I Need a Website if I Have Facebook? Honest Answer (2026)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/do-i-need-a-website-if-i-have-facebook.html

Is a Facebook or Instagram page enough for your business? Why social media alone loses you customers, and what a website does that social profiles can't.

Plenty of successful small businesses run entirely on a Facebook page or an Instagram account. It's free, it's familiar and your customers are already there. So is a website still worth it?

Short answer: yes, if you want new customers to find you. Here's why.

### Social media is rented land

Your Facebook page doesn't belong to you. The platform decides who sees your posts, can change its rules overnight, and can suspend accounts with little warning. Organic reach for business pages is a small fraction of your followers. A website is the one place online that you fully own and control.

### Google doesn't send people to your Facebook page

When someone searches "dentist near me" or "best Italian restaurant Antwerp", Google mostly shows websites and Google Business Profiles, not Facebook posts. Without a website, you are invisible to people actively searching for exactly what you offer. That is the most valuable traffic there is, because those people are ready to buy.

### A website builds trust in seconds

Customers check you out before they call. A clean, professional website with your services, opening hours, real photos and reviews tells them you are established and serious. A business with only a social profile can look temporary, especially to older customers and to other businesses.

### What a website does that social media can't

- Appear in Google search for your services and your area.

- Take bookings, orders and payments directly, without commission to a third-party platform.

- Answer questions 24/7 with an [AI assistant](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html), so you don't lose leads after closing time.

- Collect leads with contact and quote forms you own.

- Show everything in one place: menu, prices, portfolio, team, FAQs.

### The best setup: use both

This isn't website versus social media. Social media is where you stay in touch with people who already know you. Your website is where new customers find you and where everyone goes to take action. Link your social profiles to your website, and send every post's traffic to a page where people can book, call or buy.

### What does it take to get started?

A focused business website with a few pages can be live in a few weeks. Read [how much a website costs in Belgium](https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost-in-belgium.html) for typical price ranges, or talk to us directly.

# How Much Does a Website Cost in Belgium? (2026 Guide)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/how-much-does-a-website-cost-in-belgium.html

What a website really costs in Belgium in 2026: typical price ranges for business sites, online shops and custom builds, what drives the price, and the hidden costs to plan for.

"How much does a website cost?" is the first question almost every business owner asks us, and the honest answer is: it depends on what the website needs to do. That isn't a dodge. A one-page site for a local plumber and an online shop with 500 products are both "websites", but they are completely different projects.

This guide breaks down what websites typically cost in Belgium in 2026, what drives the price, and which running costs to budget for, so you can compare quotes with confidence.

### Typical website price ranges in Belgium

These are typical market ranges for professionally built websites in Belgium. Freelancers sit at the lower end, agencies at the higher end, and the final price always depends on scope.

| Type of website | Typical range | Good for |

| Template-based starter site (3–5 pages) | €800 – €2,000 | Freelancers, trades, small local businesses |

| Custom-designed business website | €2,000 – €6,000 | Restaurants, clinics, agencies, growing SMEs |

| Online shop (e-commerce) | €3,500 – €15,000+ | Brands selling products online |

| Web application or booking platform | €8,000 – €40,000+ | Custom tools, portals, SaaS products |

If you get a quote far below these ranges, ask what is not included. If you get one far above, ask what you get that justifies it.

### What actually drives the price

#### 1. Number of pages and amount of content

Every page needs to be designed, built, filled with content and tested. A five-page site is a different job from a thirty-page site with a blog and team profiles. If you supply your own text and photos, the price drops; if you need copywriting and photography, it goes up.

#### 2. Custom design vs a template

A template gets you online fast and cheaply, but you look like many other businesses using the same theme. A custom design is built around your brand and your customers, which takes more hours and costs more, but usually converts visitors into enquiries much better.

#### 3. Features and integrations

Online booking, payments, multilingual content, customer accounts, CRM connections, an [AI assistant that answers customers 24/7](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html): each feature adds development and testing time. This is often the biggest difference between two quotes that look similar on paper.

#### 4. SEO and performance

A site that loads in one second and is built to be found on Google takes more care than one that just looks nice. Ask every agency whether technical SEO (page speed, structured data, meta tags, Search Console setup) is included, because it often isn't.

### The running costs most quotes leave out

- Domain name: around €10–€30 per year for a .be or .com.

- Hosting: anywhere from €5 to €50+ per month depending on traffic and performance.

- Business email: usually a few euros per user per month.

- Maintenance: updates, backups, security and small content changes. Many agencies offer a monthly care plan for this once the site is live.

Plan for these from day one so your website keeps working long after launch.

### Cheap website vs good website: what's the real difference?

A cheap website is a cost. A good website is an investment that pays for itself. The difference shows up in three places: how fast the site loads on a phone, how easy it is for a visitor to contact or book you, and whether Google shows the site at all. If one extra customer a month covers the cost of your website within a year, it is already one of the best investments your business can make.

### How to get an accurate quote

To get a quote you can actually compare, prepare these five things before you contact an agency:

- What the website must achieve (more calls, bookings, online sales?)

- A rough list of pages you need

- Features you want: booking, payments, languages, chat

- Two or three websites you like, and why

- Your timeline and rough budget

At OptimaCoreTech we don't use a fixed price list, because no two businesses need the same thing. We start with a short call, then send a clear, tailored quote. See our [web design service in Antwerp](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html) for what's included.

# How to Choose a Web Design Agency in Antwerp: 12-Point Checklist
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-web-design-agency-in-antwerp.html

A practical checklist for choosing a web design agency in Antwerp: what to ask, what a good quote contains, red flags, and how to compare agencies before you sign.

Choosing a web design agency is one of those decisions you only notice when it goes wrong: a site that is slow, hard to update, invisible on Google, or held hostage by an agency that stopped answering emails. This checklist helps you compare agencies in Antwerp (or anywhere in Belgium) on the things that actually decide whether your website brings in customers.

### The short answer

Pick the agency that understands your business goals, shows real work similar to what you need, explains its process and timeline clearly, gives you a written quote with exactly what is included, builds for speed and SEO from day one, and leaves you owning your domain, content and accounts.

### 1. Start with your goal, not the design

Before you contact anyone, write down what the website must do: generate quote requests, take bookings, sell products, or simply make you look credible when people search your name. A good agency asks about this first. If the first conversation is only about colours and animations, that is a warning sign.

### 2. Look at real, recent work

- Ask for two or three live websites, not only screenshots.

- Open them on your phone: most of your visitors will.

- Check that they load quickly and that the contact or booking flow works.

### 3. Ask how they handle SEO

Every new website should ship with the technical basics: page titles and meta descriptions, a clean heading structure, fast loading, mobile-first layout, structured data, an XML sitemap and Google Search Console set up. If you are replacing an existing site, ask how they will keep your current Google rankings (redirects, keeping URLs and content that already rank).

### 4. Understand the process and timeline

A typical business website takes roughly 4 to 8 weeks from the first call to launch, depending on the number of pages, features and how quickly content is ready. Ask who does what, when you review designs, and what happens if you want changes.

### 5. Get a written quote that lists everything

A clear quote names the pages, features, integrations, content work, number of revision rounds, hosting and domain setup, and what happens after launch. Agencies price projects differently, so compare what is included rather than only the final number.

### 6. Make sure you own your website

Your domain, hosting account, content, images and analytics should be in your name or transferred to you. Ask this directly. It protects you if you ever want to change provider.

### 7. Ask about maintenance, but after the project

Websites need updates, backups and security checks. A good agency offers an optional care plan once the project is delivered, without making it a condition of the sale.

### 8. Check they can grow with you

Today you might need a simple site; next year you might want online booking, an app or an AI assistant that answers customers at night. Working with a team that can build websites, mobile apps and AI agents saves you from starting over with a new provider.

### 9. Local presence helps

An agency in Antwerp understands the Belgian market, can meet you in person when it matters and works in your time zone. Most of the work still happens online, so you are not limited to agencies on your street.

### 10. Read reviews and talk to a client

Google reviews are a good start. If the project is important, ask the agency whether you can speak to one of their clients.

### 11. Watch for red flags

- A guaranteed number-one position on Google. Nobody can honestly promise that.

- No written scope, or a price given before they understand your needs.

- They keep the domain or hosting in their own name with no transfer option.

- No examples you can open and test yourself.

### 12. Compare two or three agencies

Send the same short brief to each one and compare their questions, their proposal and how clearly they explain it. The quality of the questions often tells you more than the portfolio.

### How OptimaCoreTech works

OptimaCoreTech is a web design, app and AI agent studio in Antwerp that has worked with more than 50 businesses. We start with a short call about your goals, send a tailored quote (no fixed packages), design before we build, set up technical SEO and Google Search Console on every site, and offer optional care plans after launch. See our [web design service in Antwerp](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html) or [ask for a free quote](https://www.optimacoretech.com/contact-us.html).

### Frequently asked questions

#### How long does it take to build a website in Belgium?

Most business websites take about 4 to 8 weeks from the first call to launch, depending on the number of pages, features and how quickly content is ready.

#### What should a web design quote include?

The pages and features, integrations, content work, number of revision rounds, hosting and domain setup, SEO basics and what happens after launch.

#### Can a web design agency guarantee first place on Google?

No. An honest agency builds the technical foundation Google rewards, such as speed, mobile-first design, structured data and clean content, but nobody can guarantee rankings.

# Restaurant Website: 10 Things Every Restaurant Site Needs (2026)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/restaurant-website-what-to-include.html

What should a restaurant website include? Menu, online reservations, opening hours, Google Maps, reviews and more: a practical checklist for restaurant owners.

When people decide where to eat, they look you up first. Your restaurant website has one job: turn that hungry searcher into a booked table or an order. Here are the ten things every restaurant site needs.

### 1. Your menu, readable on a phone

The menu is the most visited page on any restaurant website. Put it on a real web page, not just a PDF: it loads faster, works better on phones and can be read by Google. Include prices and mark dietary options such as vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free.

### 2. Online reservations

Let guests book in two taps, at any hour. Every booking that comes in at 11 pm while you're closed is a table you would otherwise have lost. A reservation system on your own site also avoids paying commission on every cover.

### 3. Opening hours, kept up to date

Wrong opening hours lose you customers and trust. Show them clearly on every page and update them for holidays.

### 4. Location and directions

Add your full address, an embedded map, parking tips and public transport options. Make the address tappable so it opens directly in Google Maps.

### 5. A tap-to-call phone number

Many guests still prefer to call. Put a clickable phone number at the top of the site on mobile.

### 6. Real, mouth-watering photos

Professional photos of your dishes and your space do more selling than any text. Avoid stock photos; guests can tell.

### 7. Reviews and social proof

Show your best reviews and link to your Google and TripAdvisor profiles. Social proof reassures first-time visitors.

### 8. Takeaway and delivery ordering

If you do takeaway, let customers order directly from your website. You keep the margin that delivery platforms would otherwise take.

### 9. An answer for every question, even at midnight

"Do you have a terrace?" "Can I bring my dog?" "Is there a kids' menu?" An [AI assistant](https://www.optimacoretech.com/ai-agents.html) can answer these instantly and take the reservation in the same conversation.

### 10. Local SEO basics

Use your cuisine and city in your page titles ("Italian Restaurant in Antwerp"), keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere online, and connect your site to your Google Business Profile.

### Next step

A great restaurant website doesn't need to be huge. It needs to be fast, mobile-friendly and built to convert. Explore our [web design service](https://www.optimacoretech.com/web-design-antwerp.html) or our [guide to AI receptionists](https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/ai-receptionist-for-small-business.html).

# 7 Signs Your Website Is Losing You Customers (And How to Fix It)
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/signs-your-website-is-losing-customers.html

Slow loading, no mobile layout, no clear call to action: seven warning signs your business website is costing you customers, and how to fix each one.

An outdated website doesn't just look bad. It quietly sends customers to your competitors. Most business owners never notice, because lost visitors don't complain; they simply leave. Here are seven warning signs to check today.

### 1. It takes more than three seconds to load

Most visitors abandon a page that takes longer than about three seconds to load on mobile. Large images, cheap hosting and bloated themes are the usual culprits. Test your site with Google's free PageSpeed Insights tool.

### 2. It's hard to use on a phone

Most local searches happen on smartphones. If visitors have to pinch and zoom, or buttons are too small to tap, they leave. Google also ranks sites based on their mobile version, so a poor mobile experience hurts your rankings too.

### 3. Visitors can't tell what you do within five seconds

Your homepage should answer three questions immediately: what you offer, who it's for and where you are. Vague slogans like "Innovative solutions for tomorrow" don't do that. Be specific.

### 4. There's no clear next step

Every page needs one obvious action: call, book, request a quote or buy. If your phone number is hidden in the footer and there is no booking button, you're making customers work too hard.

### 5. It doesn't show up on Google

Search for your main service plus your city. If you can't find yourself, neither can your customers. Common causes are missing page titles, no local information, thin content and technical errors that stop Google from indexing the site.

### 6. The information is out of date

Old opening hours, past events, a copyright year from five years ago or broken links all tell visitors the business might not be active. Keep your site current, or have someone maintain it for you.

### 7. It doesn't build trust

No real photos, no reviews, no team, no address: visitors can't tell if you're legitimate. Show your work, your people and what your customers say about you.

### How to fix it

Some of these are quick fixes; others are a sign it's time for a redesign. A modern website built for speed, mobile and search will usually outperform an old one within months. # Website Redesign Without Losing Google Rankings: SEO Checklist
URL: https://www.optimacoretech.com/blog/website-redesign-without-losing-google-rankings.html

Redesigning your website? Keep your Google rankings with this SEO checklist: URLs, redirects, content, metadata, structured data, speed and what to check after launch.

A new design can make your business look years younger. Done carelessly, it can also wipe out the Google traffic you spent years building. The good news: rankings depend on a short list of things you can protect during a redesign.

### The short answer

Keep the URLs and content that already rank, redirect every URL that changes, carry over titles, descriptions and structured data, keep or improve page speed, and check Google Search Console closely in the weeks after launch.

### Before the redesign

- Export what ranks today. In Google Search Console, list the pages and search queries that bring clicks. These pages are your priority.

- Crawl the current site. Save every URL, page title, meta description and heading so nothing gets lost.

- Decide the new structure. Keep URLs the same wherever you can. Every change needs a redirect.

### During the build

- Keep the content that ranks. You can rewrite and improve it, but don't delete the topics and answers Google sends people to.

- Carry over the metadata. Page titles, meta descriptions, canonical tags and Open Graph tags should move to the new pages unchanged unless you improve them on purpose.

- Keep structured data. Organization, LocalBusiness, FAQ, breadcrumb and article markup help Google and AI assistants understand who you are.

- One H1 per page, with headings that describe the content.

- Mind the speed. New designs often add heavy images, videos and scripts. Compress images, lazy-load what is below the fold and test on a phone.

- Don't forget internal links between related pages and articles.

### At launch

- Set up 301 redirects for every URL that changed and test them.

- Remove any "noindex" left over from the staging site.

- Submit the updated XML sitemap in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

- Check that analytics and conversion tracking still work.

### After launch

Watch Search Console for crawl errors, pages that drop out of the index and queries that lose clicks. Small dips in the first weeks are normal while Google re-crawls; a sharp drop on one page usually points to a missing redirect or lost content.

### Mistakes we see most often

- Changing every URL without redirects.

- Replacing detailed pages with short, design-led pages that say less.

- Losing page titles and descriptions because the new template generates generic ones.

- Launching with images several megabytes in size.

### How OptimaCoreTech handles redesigns

When OptimaCoreTech redesigns a site, the existing titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs and structured data are carried over and checked page by page before launch, so the new design keeps the search visibility the old one earned. ### Frequently asked questions

#### Will a website redesign hurt my SEO?

Not if you keep the URLs and content that rank, redirect any URL that changes, carry over titles, descriptions and structured data, and monitor Google Search Console after launch.

#### Do I need redirects when I redesign my website?

Yes. Every URL that changes needs a 301 redirect to its new address, otherwise Google and visitors land on error pages and rankings can drop.

#### How long does it take for rankings to settle after a redesign?

Small changes in the first weeks are normal while Google re-crawls the site. A sharp, lasting drop on a page usually points to a missing redirect or lost content.
